The provided documents detail the technical specifications, optimization campaigns, and user documentation for **Strata**, a local inference engine designed to run large language models (LLMs) on consumer hardware. The materials primarily focus on two distinct areas: a rigorous performance optimization campaign for Intel Arc GPUs and general product documentation for end-users and developers.

**Intel Arc A770 Optimization Campaign**
The core technical document, `A770_SPEED_SPEC.md`, outlines an effort to achieve at least 20 tokens/second (tok/s) in decode throughput on an Intel Arc A770 GPU using the Strata SYCL engine. The target model is Qwen3.8-Flash-Next Coder IQ1_M. The campaign begins with a baseline of ~9–11 tok/s and systematically tests various optimization levers, including kernel tuning, memory management, and architectural changes.

Initial work packages focused on reliable event-based measurements and BF16 projection paths. Microbenchmarks revealed that the default `bf16_gemv_fp32_mmvf_multi` path was superior to row-based alternatives, which were 1.4–6x slower. Register allocation tuning (GRF sizes) proved ineffective, with larger register files causing significant slowdowns. Consequently, the BF16 projection family was ruled out as the primary bottleneck.
